chapter_title: Improving a Resource with AI Agents
learning_objective: The learner will identify the six common errors of a PDF-to-Markdown conversion from a description of how each looks, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** pdf-conversion-error-poster
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the six common errors of a PDF-to-Markdown conversion from a description of how each looks, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** PDF-to-Markdown Conversion (defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A conversion that opens without an error is correct. (2) A tool converts every element equally well. (3) Only text can be lost. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying conversion errors is a Remember-level task, and a picture of a converted page with the errors marked gives each one a place and a look. The quiz asks the learner to recognize an error by its appearance. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of a converted page. The page has a large heading bar at the top. Below it are two columns of thin lines, with lines from the left column running into lines from the right column. Under the columns is a grid of cells whose lines have collapsed into one stack. To the right is a row of scrambled small symbols where a formula should be. Below that is an empty frame with a dashed outline where a picture should be. At the bottom is a thin line with a short hyphen inside one word. The six markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Lost heading | The large bar at the top that has shrunk to the same weight as plain lines. | A heading that has become plain text. | List the headings in the output and compare with the original. | | 2 | Column order | The two columns whose lines run into each other. | Lines from two columns are mixed together. | Read one paragraph from each column in the output. | | 3 | Flattened table | The grid of cells whose lines have collapsed into one stack. | A table whose rows and columns are lost. | Compare each table with the original. | | 4 | Garbled equation | The row of scrambled small symbols. | A formula that no longer reads correctly. | Compare each formula with the original. | | 5 | Lost image | The empty frame with a dashed outline. | A picture that is missing, with no note. | Count the pictures before and after. | | 6 | Split word | The thin line with a short hyphen inside one word. | A word broken at a line end that stayed broken. | Search for stray hyphens inside words. | **Provenance:** The six errors follow the chapter section "PDF-to-Markdown Conversion". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the page "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 6 from the top of the page to its bottom. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 6 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can spot a conversion error." Below 5 it lists the labels of the missed errors. **Starting State:** The illustration with six numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what went wrong." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of conversion errors lists the same six errors, in a different order, with a check for each.
